arabic: مرّ وقت طويل دون مطر، فجفّت البرك الصغيرة وقلّ الماء.
english_before: A long time passed without rain, the small ponds dried up, and water became scarce.
english_after: A long time passed without rain, the small ponds dried up, and water became scarce.

arabic: شعرت الفيلة بعطش شديد، وبدأت تبحث عن مكان جديد تشرب منه.
english_before: The elephants grew very thirsty and began searching for a new place to drink.
english_after: The elephants grew very thirsty and began searching for a new place to drink.

arabic: بعد رحلة طويلة، وجد أحد الفيلة بحيرة جميلة.
english_before: After a long journey, one elephant found a beautiful lake.
english_after: After a long journey, one elephant found a beautiful lake.

arabic: كانت الأرانب الصغيرة تعيش حولها، في بيوت تحت الأرض.
english_before: Little hares lived all around it in homes beneath the ground.
english_after: Little hares lived all around it in homes beneath the ground.

arabic: أسرعت الفيلة نحو الماء، دون أن تنتبه إلى جحور الأرانب.
english_before: The elephants hurried toward the water without noticing the hares’ burrows.
english_after: The elephants hurried toward the water without noticing the hares’ burrows.

arabic: كانت خطوات الفيلة ثقيلة،
english_before: The elephants’ footsteps were heavy.
english_after: The elephants’ footsteps were heavy.

arabic: فهدمت بعض الجحور وأخافت الأرانب.
english_before: They damaged some burrows and frightened the hares.
english_after: They destroyed some burrows and frightened the hares.

arabic: تجمعت الأرانب في مكان بعيد، وقالت:
english_before: The hares gathered far away and said,
english_after: The hares gathered far away and said,

arabic: «إذا عادت الفيلة كل يوم، فلن يبقى لنا بيت آمن.»
english_before: “If the elephants return every day, we will have no safe homes left.”
english_after: “If the elephants return every day, we will have no safe homes left.”

arabic: قال أرنب ذكي: «سأتحدث إلى ملك الفيلة،
english_before: A clever hare said, “I will speak to the king of the elephants,
english_after: A clever hare said, “I will speak to the king of the elephants,

arabic: لكنني لن أقترب من قدميه.»
english_before: but I will not go near his feet.”
english_after: but I will not go near his feet.”

arabic: وفي المساء، صعد فوق صخرة عالية،
english_before: That evening he climbed onto a high rock
english_after: That evening he climbed onto a high rock

arabic: ونادى ملك الفيلة بصوت يسمعه الجميع.
english_before: and called to the elephant king in a voice everyone could hear.
english_after: and called to the elephant king in a voice everyone could hear.

arabic: قال الأرنب: «أنا رسول القمر!
english_before: “I am the messenger of the moon!” the hare declared.
english_after: “I am the messenger of the moon!” the hare declared.

arabic: إن هذه البحيرة تخصّ القمر،
english_before: “This lake belongs to the moon,
english_after: “This lake belongs to the moon,

arabic: وقد غضب لأنكم آذيتم الأرانب التي تعيش بجانبها.»
english_before: and he is angry because you have hurt the hares who live beside it.”
english_after: and he is angry because you have hurt the hares who live beside it.”

arabic: توقف ملك الفيلة متعجبًا، وسأل: «وأين أرى القمر؟»
english_before: The elephant king stopped in surprise and asked, “Where can I see the moon?”
english_after: The elephant king stopped in surprise and asked, “Where can I see the moon?”

arabic: أخذه الأرنب إلى حافة البحيرة في ليلة صافية.
english_before: The hare led him to the lake’s edge on a clear night.
english_after: The hare led him to the lake’s edge on a clear night.

arabic: كان القمر يلمع في السماء، وتظهر صورته على سطح الماء.
english_before: The moon was shining in the sky, and its reflection appeared on the surface of the water.
english_after: The moon was shining in the sky, and its reflection appeared on the surface of the water.

arabic: قال الأرنب: «انظر إلى القمر هنا، ولا تزعجه.»
english_before: “Look at the moon here,” said the hare, “and do not disturb him.”
english_after: “Look at the moon here,” said the hare, “and do not disturb him.”

arabic: انحنى ملك الفيلة ليرى الصورة، فحرّك الماء بخرطومه دون قصد.
english_before: The elephant king bent down to look at the reflection and accidentally stirred the water with his trunk.
english_after: The elephant king bent down to look at the reflection and accidentally stirred the water with his trunk.

arabic: اهتزت صورة القمر واختفت لحظة.
english_before: The moon’s image shook and disappeared for a moment.
english_after: The moon’s image shook and disappeared for a moment.

arabic: قال الأرنب: «أرأيت؟ لقد أغضبته مرة أخرى!»
english_before: “See?” said the hare. “You have angered him again!”
english_after: “See?” said the hare. “You have angered him again!”

arabic: خاف الملك وتراجع إلى الخلف.
english_before: The king grew afraid and stepped back.
english_after: The king grew afraid and stepped back.

arabic: جمع ملك الفيلة قطيعه وقال:
english_before: The elephant king gathered his herd and said,
english_after: The elephant king gathered his herd and said,

arabic: «سنبحث عن ماء في مكان آخر، ولن نؤذي هذه الأرانب.»
english_before: “We will find water somewhere else, and we will not harm these hares.”
english_after: “We will find water somewhere else, and we will not harm these hares.”

arabic: رحلت الفيلة في الصباح.
english_before: The elephants left in the morning.
english_after: The elephants left in the morning.

arabic: وعادت الأرانب إلى جحورها، وفرحت لأن بيوتها أصبحت آمنة من جديد.
english_before: The hares returned to their burrows, happy that their homes were safe once more.
english_after: The hares returned to their burrows, happy that their homes were safe once more.

arabic: في يوم من الأيام، ذهب ناسك إلى السوق واشترى ماعزًا سمينًا.
english_before: One day, an ascetic went to the market and bought a fat goat.
english_after: One day, an ascetic went to the market and bought a fat goat.

arabic: دفع ثمنه، وربط حبلًا حول رقبته،
english_before: He paid for it, tied a rope around its neck,
english_after: He paid for it, tied a rope around its neck,

arabic: ثم بدأ يمشي به إلى بيته.
english_before: and started walking home with it.
english_after: and started walking home with it.

arabic: كان سعيدًا بما اشتراه، ولم يشك في شيء.
english_before: He was pleased with his purchase and suspected nothing.
english_after: He was pleased with his purchase and suspected nothing.

arabic: رأى ثلاثة لصوص الماعز، وأرادوا أخذه دون أن يدفعوا مالًا.
english_before: Three thieves saw the goat and wanted to take it without paying.
english_after: Three thieves saw the goat and wanted to take it without paying.

arabic: اجتمعوا خلف شجرة، واتفقوا على حيلة غريبة.
english_before: They met behind a tree and agreed on a strange trick.
english_after: They met behind a tree and agreed on a strange trick.

arabic: قال أحدهم: «لن نسرق الماعز بالقوة.
english_before: One said, “We will not steal the goat by force.
english_after: One said, “We will not steal the goat by force.

arabic: سنجعل الرجل يتركه بنفسه.»
english_before: We will make the man abandon it himself.”
english_after: We will make the man abandon it himself.”

arabic: وقف اللص الأول عند الطريق،
english_before: The first thief stood by the road.
english_after: The first thief stood by the road.

arabic: وحين مر الناسك سأله بدهشة: «لماذا تقود كلبًا إلى بيتك؟»
english_before: When the ascetic passed, he asked in surprise, “Why are you leading a dog home?”
english_after: When the ascetic passed, he asked in surprise, “Why are you leading a dog home?”

arabic: ضحك الناسك وقال: «هذا ماعز، وليس كلبًا!
english_before: The ascetic laughed. “This is a goat, not a dog!
english_after: The ascetic laughed. “This is a goat, not a dog!

arabic: ألا ترى جيدًا؟» ثم واصل طريقه.
english_before: Can you not see properly?” Then he continued on his way.
english_after: Can you not see properly?” Then he continued on his way.

arabic: بعد قليل، ظهر اللص الثاني، ونظر إلى الماعز مستغربًا.
english_before: A little later, the second thief appeared and stared at the goat in astonishment.
english_after: A little later, the second thief appeared and stared at the goat in astonishment.

arabic: قال: «رجل مثلك يقود كلبًا في الشارع؟ هذا أمر عجيب!»
english_before: “A man like you leading a dog through the street? How strange!” he said.
english_after: “A man like you leading a dog through the street? How strange!” he said.

arabic: توقف الناسك وقال لنفسه: «لماذا يسميه الجميع كلبًا؟»
english_before: The ascetic stopped and wondered, “Why does everyone call it a dog?”
english_after: The ascetic stopped and wondered, “Why does everyone call it a dog?”

arabic: ثم جاء اللص الثالث، وقال بصوت واثق:
english_before: Then the third thief came and said confidently,
english_after: Then the third thief came and said confidently,

arabic: «يا رجل، هذا كلب بلا شك. من باعه لك؟»
english_before: “My good man, that is certainly a dog. Who sold it to you?”
english_after: “My good man, that is certainly a dog. Who sold it to you?”

arabic: نظر الناسك إلى الحيوان مرة أخرى،
english_before: The ascetic looked at the animal again
english_after: The ascetic looked at the animal again

arabic: وبدأ يشعر بالقلق والحيرة.
english_before: and began to feel worried and confused.
english_after: and began to feel worried and confused.

arabic: فكر الناسك: «أنا رأيت ماعزًا في السوق،
english_before: The ascetic thought, “I saw a goat at the market,
english_after: The ascetic thought, “I saw a goat at the market,

arabic: لكن ثلاثة رجال يقولون إنه كلب.
english_before: but three men say it is a dog.
english_after: but three men say it is a dog.

arabic: هل خدعني البائع؟ أم أنني لا أرى الحقيقة؟»
english_before: Did the seller deceive me? Or can I no longer see the truth?”
english_after: Did the seller deceive me? Or am I not seeing the truth?"

arabic: ولم يعرف أي كلام يصدق.
english_before: He did not know whom to believe.
english_after: He did not know whom to believe.

arabic: أخيرًا، أقنع نفسه أن البائع ربما سحر عينيه.
english_before: At last, he convinced himself that perhaps the seller had cast a spell on his eyes.
english_after: At last, he convinced himself that perhaps the seller had cast a spell on his eyes.

arabic: فك الحبل عن رقبة الماعز، وتركه عند جانب الطريق،
english_before: He untied the rope, left the goat beside the road,
english_after: He untied the rope from the goat's neck and left it beside the road,

arabic: ثم عاد إلى السوق غاضبًا ليبحث عن الرجل الذي باعه له.
english_before: and returned angrily to the market to look for the seller.
english_after: and returned angrily to the market to look for the seller.

arabic: خرج اللصوص الثلاثة من أماكنهم، وأمسكوا الماعز ومضوا به.
english_before: The three thieves emerged from their hiding places, took the goat, and went away.
english_after: The three thieves emerged from their hiding places, took the goat, and went away.

arabic: كانوا يضحكون لأن خطتهم نجحت دون صراع.
english_before: They laughed because their plan had worked without a struggle.
english_after: They laughed because their plan had worked without a struggle.

arabic: أما الناسك فكان يبحث عن البائع،
english_before: The ascetic, meanwhile, was looking for the seller,
english_after: The ascetic, meanwhile, was looking for the seller,

arabic: ولا يعلم أن الماعز كان ماعزًا طوال الوقت.
english_before: unaware that his goat had been a goat all along.
english_after: unaware that his goat had been a goat all along.

arabic: كان ناسك يجلس قرب نهر، فرأى طائرًا يحمل فأرة صغيرة في مخالبه.
english_before: An ascetic was sitting beside a river when he saw a bird carrying a little mouse in its claws.
english_after: An ascetic was sitting beside a river when he saw a bird carrying a little mouse in its claws.

arabic: سقطت الفأرة من الطائر أمامه، فحملها برفق.
english_before: The mouse fell in front of him, and he picked her up gently.
english_after: The mouse fell in front of him, and he picked her up gently.

arabic: أراد أن يحميها، فدعا الله أن تصبح فتاة تستطيع العيش في بيته.
english_before: Wanting to protect her, he prayed that she might become a girl and live in his home.
english_after: Wanting to protect her, he prayed that she might become a girl and live in his home.

arabic: تحولت الفأرة إلى طفلة جميلة، وأخذها الناسك إلى زوجته.
english_before: The mouse turned into a beautiful little girl, and the ascetic took her to his wife.
english_after: The mouse turned into a beautiful little girl, and the ascetic took her to his wife.

arabic: ربياها كأنها ابنتهما، ومرت سنوات كثيرة حتى صارت شابة.
english_before: They raised her as their own daughter. Many years passed, and she grew into a young woman.
english_after: They raised her as their own daughter. Many years passed, and she grew into a young woman.

arabic: وفي يوم، سألها أبوها عن الرجل الذي تريد الزواج منه.
english_before: One day, her father asked whom she wanted to marry.
english_after: One day, her father asked whom she wanted to marry.

arabic: قالت الفتاة: «أريد زوجًا أقوى من الجميع.»
english_before: “I want a husband stronger than everyone,” the young woman said.
english_after: “I want a husband stronger than everyone,” the young woman said.

arabic: فكر الأب قليلًا، ثم قال: «إذن اسألي الشمس.
english_before: Her father thought for a moment. “Then ask the sun,” he said.
english_after: Her father thought for a moment. “Then ask the sun,” he said.

arabic: إنها تضيء العالم كله، ولا نعرف شيئًا أقوى منها.»
english_before: “It lights the whole world, and we know nothing stronger.”
english_after: “It lights the whole world, and we know nothing stronger.”

arabic: فذهبا إلى الشمس.
english_before: So they went to the sun.
english_after: So they went to the sun.

arabic: لكن الشمس قالت: «السحاب أقوى مني، لأنه يستطيع أن يحجب نوري.»
english_before: But the sun said, “The cloud is stronger than I am, because it can block my light.”
english_after: But the sun said, “The cloud is stronger than I am, because it can block my light.”

arabic: ذهبا إلى السحاب، فقال: «الريح أقوى مني.
english_before: They went to the cloud, which said, “The wind is stronger than I am.
english_after: They went to the cloud, which said, “The wind is stronger than I am.

arabic: إنها تدفعني من مكان إلى آخر، ولا أستطيع مقاومتها.»
english_before: It pushes me from one place to another, and I cannot resist it.”
english_after: It pushes me from one place to another, and I cannot resist it.”

arabic: سألا الريح، فقالت: «الجبل أقوى مني.
english_before: They asked the wind, which said, “The mountain is stronger than I am.
english_after: They asked the wind, which said, “The mountain is stronger than I am.

arabic: أستطيع تحريك السحاب والأشجار، لكن الجبل يبقى ثابتًا مهما هببت.»
english_before: I can move clouds and trees, but the mountain stays in place however hard I blow.”
english_after: I can move clouds and trees, but the mountain stays in place however hard I blow.”

arabic: فرحت الفتاة، وذهبت مع أبيها إلى الجبل الكبير.
english_before: The young woman was pleased, and she and her father went to the great mountain.
english_after: The young woman was pleased, and she and her father went to the great mountain.

arabic: قال الجبل: «هناك مخلوق صغير أقوى مني.
english_before: The mountain said, “There is a little creature stronger than I am: the mouse.
english_after: The mountain said, "There is a little creature stronger than I am.
note: added 'the mouse', which belongs to next chunk

arabic: إنه الفأر الذي يحفر داخل الصخور، ويصنع لنفسه بيتًا في جسمي.
english_before: He digs into the rocks and makes a home inside me.
english_after: It is the mouse, who digs inside the rocks and makes himself a home in my body.
note: omitted 'it is the mouse' and 'in my body'

arabic: لا أقدر على منعه.»
english_before: I cannot stop him.”
english_after: I cannot stop him.”

arabic: نظرت الفتاة إلى أبيها بدهشة.
english_before: The young woman looked at her father in surprise.
english_after: The young woman looked at her father in surprise.

arabic: وجدا فأرًا قرب الجبل،
english_before: They found a mouse near the mountain,
english_after: They found a mouse near the mountain,

arabic: وسأله الناسك: «هل تتزوج ابنتي؟»
english_before: and the ascetic asked, “Will you marry my daughter?”
english_after: and the ascetic asked, “Will you marry my daughter?”

arabic: قال الفأر: «لكنها إنسانة، وبيتي صغير جدًا.
english_before: The mouse replied, “But she is human, and my home is very small.
english_after: The mouse replied, “But she is human, and my home is very small.

arabic: أستطيع الزواج من فأرة مثلي، لا من إنسانة.»
english_before: I can marry a mouse like myself, not a human.”
english_after: I can marry a mouse like myself, not a human.”

arabic: ابتسمت الفتاة وقالت لأبيها:
english_before: The young woman smiled and told her father,
english_after: The young woman smiled and told her father,

arabic: «أريد أن أعود فأرة كما كنت، وأتزوج هذا الفأر.»
english_before: “I want to become a mouse again, as I once was, and marry this mouse.”
english_after: “I want to become a mouse again, as I once was, and marry this mouse.”

arabic: وافق الأب، فتحولت إلى فأرة من جديد.
english_before: Her father agreed, and she turned back into a mouse.
english_after: Her father agreed, and she turned back into a mouse.

arabic: دخلت بيت الفأر، وانتهت رحلتها الطويلة عند الجبل.
english_before: She entered the mouse’s home, and her long journey ended beside the mountain.
english_after: She entered the mouse’s home, and her long journey ended beside the mountain.

arabic: عاش ناسك في بيت صغير،
english_before: An ascetic lived in a small house
english_after: An ascetic lived in a small house

arabic: وكان يحصل كل يوم على قليل من السمن والعسل.
english_before: and received a little ghee and honey each day.
english_after: and received a little ghee and honey each day.

arabic: يأكل ما يحتاج إليه، ويضع الباقي في جرّة من الفخار.
english_before: He ate what he needed and put the rest in a clay jar.
english_after: He ate what he needed and put the rest in a clay jar.

arabic: ومع مرور الأيام، امتلأت الجرّة تقريبًا.
english_before: As the days passed, the jar became almost full.
english_after: As the days passed, the jar became almost full.

arabic: ذات مساء، جلس الناسك تحت الجرّة المعلقة فوق رأسه.
english_before: One evening, the ascetic sat beneath the jar hanging above his head.
english_after: One evening, the ascetic sat beneath the jar hanging above his head.

arabic: نظر إليها وقال: «كم فيها من السمن والعسل!
english_before: He looked at it and said, “There is so much ghee and honey in there!
english_after: He looked at it and said, “There is so much ghee and honey in there!

arabic: لو بعتهما في السوق، لحصلت على مال كثير.»
english_before: If I sold them at the market, I would get plenty of money.”
english_after: If I sold them at the market, I would get plenty of money.”

arabic: وبدأ يحسب الأرباح في خياله.
english_before: He began calculating imaginary profits.
english_after: He began calculating imaginary profits.

arabic: قال في نفسه: «سأشتري بهذا المال بعض الماعز.
english_before: He thought, “With that money I will buy some goats.
english_after: He thought, “With that money I will buy some goats.

arabic: وبعد أشهر ستولد لها صغار، ويكبر القطيع.
english_before: After a few months, they will have young, and the herd will grow.
english_after: After a few months, they will have young, and the herd will grow.

arabic: ثم أبيع بعضه، وأشتري أبقارًا وحقلًا واسعًا.»
english_before: Then I will sell some and buy cows and a wide field.”
english_after: Then I will sell some and buy cows and a wide field.”

arabic: ابتسم وهو يتخيل ذلك.
english_before: He smiled as he imagined it.
english_after: He smiled as he imagined it.

arabic: ثم قال: «سأزرع الحقل وأجمع المحصول،
english_before: Then he said, “I will plant the field and gather the harvest.
english_after: Then he said, “I will plant the field and gather the harvest.

arabic: ويصبح عندي طعام ومال.
english_before: I will have food and money.
english_after: I will have food and money.

arabic: سأبني بيتًا كبيرًا، وأشتري أثاثًا جميلًا، ويعرف الناس أنني رجل غني.»
english_before: I will build a big house, buy beautiful furniture, and everyone will know I am a rich man.”
english_after: I will build a big house, buy beautiful furniture, and everyone will know I am a rich man.”

arabic: كان حلمه يكبر كل لحظة.
english_before: His dream grew with every moment.
english_after: His dream grew with every moment.

arabic: لم يتوقف خياله عند ذلك.
english_before: His imagination did not stop there.
english_after: His imagination did not stop there.

arabic: تخيل أنه تزوج، وأن زوجته أنجبت ولدًا ذكيًا.
english_before: He pictured himself married, with a clever son.
english_after: He imagined that he had married, and that his wife had borne a clever son.
note: omitted that his wife bore the son

arabic: قال: «سأعلم ابني القراءة والحساب،
english_before: “I will teach my son reading and arithmetic,” he said.
english_after: “I will teach my son reading and arithmetic,” he said.

arabic: وعندما يكبر سيعمل في قصر الملك، ويفتخر الناس به.»
english_before: “When he grows up, he will work in the king’s palace, and people will be proud of him.”
english_after: “When he grows up, he will work in the king’s palace, and people will be proud of him.”

english_after: Then he imagined that one day his son disobeyed him.

english_after: even the honey he had saved was gone.

english_after: A dove built a nest high in a palm tree beside a river.

english_after: She fed them each day and rarely left the nest.

arabic: وفي صباح، وقف ثعلب تحت النخلة وصاح:

english_after: One morning, a fox stood beneath the palm tree and shouted,

english_after: “Give me one of your chicks, or I will climb up and eat all of you!”

english_after: The dove was frightened. She thought he could reach her,

english_after: so she dropped one chick to him.

english_after: The fox came back a few days later and threatened her again.

arabic: ففعلت الحمامة الشيء نفسه، وحزنت حزنًا شديدًا.
english_before: The dove did the same thing and was deeply distressed.
english_after: The dove did the same thing and was deeply distressed.

english_after: A heron saw her near the river

english_after: and asked why she was crying.

english_after: The fox came the next day and repeated his threat.

arabic: هذه المرة أجابته الحمامة بثبات:

english_after: This time the dove answered firmly,

english_after: “Climb up yourself if you can! I will not throw anything to you.”

english_after: Then the fox asked,

english_after: “And what do you do if the wind comes from every direction?”

arabic: قال مالك الحزين: «أضع رأسي تحت جناحي.»

english_after: The heron said, “I put my head under my wing.”

english_after: The fox asked him to demonstrate, and the bird agreed.

arabic: وما إن أخفى مالك الحزين رأسه تحت جناحه،

english_after: As soon as the heron tucked his head beneath his wing,

english_after: the fox leaped on him and caught him.

arabic: قال ساخرًا: «عرفت كيف تنصح الحمامة، لكنك لم تعرف كيف تحمي نفسك!»
english_before: “You knew how to advise the dove,” he mocked, “but not how to protect yourself!”
english_after: “You knew how to advise the dove,” he mocked, “but not how to protect yourself!”

english_after: Then he ate him and went away, leaving the river quiet.

arabic: عمل خادم في بيت رجل غني، وكان يعرف كل غرفة وكل باب فيه.

english_after: His friend came inside whenever the owners went out,

english_after: and they sold what they took and divided the money.

english_after: The friend arrived, and the two began putting valuable things into bags.

english_before: “Quick! Escape through the back door by the well!” and pointed the way.

english_before: The thief ran to the back and found the open door.
english_after: The thief ran to the back and found the open door.

arabic: لكنه لم يرَ بئرًا بجانبه.

english_before: He hurried back to the servant and said,
english_after: He hurried back to the servant and said,

english_before: “I found the door, but where is the well you mentioned?”
english_after: “I found the door, but where is the well you mentioned?”

arabic: قال الخادم: «لم أذكر البئر إلا لتعرف مكان الباب!
english_before: “I mentioned the well only to help you find the door!” the servant said.
english_after: “I mentioned the well only to help you find the door!” the servant said.

arabic: إذا وجدته، فاخرج فورًا!»
english_before: “Once you find it, go out immediately!”

arabic: بحثت عنها ولم أجدها. كيف أخرج دون أن أراها؟»
english_before: I looked and could not find it. How can I leave without seeing it?”
english_after: I looked and could not find it. How can I leave without seeing it?”

english_after: The servant begged his friend, “Forget the well!

english_after: He saw bags filled with his belongings and then the two men arguing.

arabic: وفي يوم، مرض ابن الملك مرضًا شديدًا.
english_before: One day the king’s son fell gravely ill.
english_after: One day the king’s son fell gravely ill.

arabic: أحضروا الطبيب العجوز، فسأل الشاب عن ألمه وأعراضه.
english_before: They brought the old physician, who asked the young man about his pain and symptoms.
english_after: They brought the old physician, who asked the young man about his pain and symptoms.

arabic: فكر قليلًا، ثم عرف المرض وشرح الدواء الذي يحتاج إليه،
english_before: After thinking, he recognized the illness and described the needed medicine,
english_after: After thinking, he recognized the illness and described the needed medicine,

arabic: لكنه رفض أن يخلطه بيده لأنه لا يرى جيدًا.
english_before: but refused to mix it himself because he could not see well.
english_after: but refused to mix it himself because he could not see well.

arabic: سمع رجل جاهل بالقصة،
english_before: An ignorant man heard the story
english_after: An ignorant man heard the story

arabic: ورأى فيها فرصة ليكسب المال ويقترب من الملك.
english_before: and saw a chance to earn money and gain the king’s favor.
english_after: and saw in it a chance to earn money and get close to the king.
note: 'gain favor' for 'get close to the king'

arabic: ذهب إلى القصر وقال بثقة:
english_before: He went to the palace and said confidently,
english_after: He went to the palace and said confidently,

arabic: «أنا طبيب، وأعرف كيف أخلط الأدوية. دعوني أجهز علاج الأمير.»
english_before: “I am a physician, and I know how to mix medicines. Let me prepare the prince’s treatment.”
english_after: “I am a physician, and I know how to mix medicines. Let me prepare the prince’s treatment.”

arabic: صدقه رجال القصر، وأدخلوه مخزن الأدوية.
english_before: The palace officials believed him and led him into the medicine store.
english_after: The palace officials believed him and led him into the medicine store.

arabic: كانت الرفوف مليئة بعلب الأعشاب والمساحيق.
english_before: The shelves were full of boxes of herbs and powders.
english_after: The shelves were full of boxes of herbs and powders.

arabic: نظر الرجل حوله، لكنه لم يعرف أسماء أكثرها
english_before: He looked around but did not know the names of most of them
english_after: He looked around but did not know the names of most of them

arabic: ولا أثرها في الجسم.
english_before: or their effects on the body.
english_after: or their effects on the body.

arabic: بدأ يأخذ قليلًا من هذه العلبة وقليلًا من تلك.
english_before: He began taking a little from one box and a little from another.
english_after: He began taking a little from one box and a little from another.

arabic: وبين الأشياء التي اختارها مسحوق سام لا يصلح للشرب.
english_before: Among the things he chose was a poisonous powder that could not be swallowed.
english_after: Among the things he chose was a poisonous powder not fit to drink.

arabic: لم يدرك خطره، فخلطه مع بقية المواد
english_before: He did not recognize the danger, mixed it with the other substances,
english_after: He did not recognize the danger, mixed it with the other substances,

arabic: وقدمه في إناء صغير.
english_before: and brought it in a small bowl.
english_after: and brought it in a small bowl.

arabic: أعجب الملك بسرعة الرجل، وظن أنها دليل على مهارته.
english_before: The king was impressed by the man’s speed and took it as a sign of skill.
english_after: The king was impressed by the man’s speed and took it as a sign of skill.

arabic: أمر أن يشرب ابنه الدواء.
english_before: He ordered his son to drink the medicine.
english_after: He ordered his son to drink the medicine.

arabic: لكن الأمير اشتد عليه الألم بعد أن شربه، ومات بعد وقت قصير.
english_before: But the prince’s pain worsened after drinking it, and he died soon afterward.
english_after: But the prince’s pain worsened after drinking it, and he died soon afterward.

arabic: عم الحزن القصر كله.
english_before: Grief filled the palace.
english_after: Grief filled the palace.

arabic: غضب الملك وسأل الرجل:
english_before: The king was furious and asked the man,
english_after: The king was furious and asked the man,
note: Arabic re-chunked at phrase boundaries (owner request); English follows

arabic: «هل أنت متأكد أن هذا هو العلاج الصحيح؟»
english_before: “Are you certain that this was the correct treatment?”
english_after: "Are you sure that this is the correct treatment?"
note: Arabic re-chunked at phrase boundaries (owner request); English follows

arabic: لم يجد الجاهل جوابًا مقنعًا.
english_before: The ignorant man had no convincing answer.
english_after: The ignorant man found no convincing answer.
note: Arabic re-chunked at phrase boundaries (owner request); English follows

arabic: عندها أمره الملك أن يشرب من الدواء نفسه الذي صنعه للأمير.
english_before: The king then ordered him to drink the very medicine he had prepared for the prince.
english_after: Then the king ordered him to drink the same medicine he had made for the prince.
note: Arabic re-chunked at phrase boundaries (owner request); English follows

arabic: شرب الرجل من الخليط، فأصابه السم ومات هو أيضًا.
english_before: The man drank the mixture, was poisoned, and died too.
english_after: The man drank the mixture, was poisoned, and died too.

arabic: بقي الطبيب العجوز حيًا، لكنه لم يستطع إعادة الأمير.
english_before: The old physician remained alive, but he could not bring the prince back.
english_after: The old physician remained alive, but he could not bring the prince back.

arabic: وكان الجميع يعرف الآن
english_before: Everyone now knew
english_after: Everyone now knew

arabic: أن الثقة الكاذبة قد قتلت شخصين.
english_before: that false confidence had cost two people their lives.
english_after: that false confidence had cost two people their lives.

arabic: حصل ناسك على بقرة حلوب، وقادها إلى بيته في المساء.
english_before: An ascetic received a milking cow and led it home in the evening.
english_after: An ascetic received a milking cow and led it home in the evening.

arabic: كان يتخيل كيف سيشرب من لبنها كل يوم.
english_before: He imagined drinking its milk every day.
english_after: He imagined drinking its milk every day.

arabic: لكن لصًا رآه في الطريق
english_before: But a thief saw him on the road
english_after: But a thief saw him on the road

arabic: وقرر أن يتبعه ليسرق البقرة عندما ينام.
english_before: and decided to follow him and steal the cow after he fell asleep.
english_after: and decided to follow him and steal the cow after he fell asleep.

arabic: في الوقت نفسه، كان شيطان يتبع الناسك أيضًا.
english_before: At the same time a devil was also following the ascetic.
english_after: At the same time a devil was also following the ascetic.

arabic: لم يكن يريد البقرة، بل أراد أن يخطف الرجل وهو نائم.
english_before: He did not want the cow; he intended to abduct the sleeping man.
english_after: He did not want the cow; he intended to abduct the sleeping man.

arabic: التقى الشيطان باللص قرب البيت،
english_before: The devil met the thief near the house,
english_after: The devil met the thief near the house,

arabic: وسأله كل واحد منهما عن سبب وجوده.
english_before: and each asked the other why he was there.
english_after: and each asked the other why he was there.

arabic: قال اللص: «سآخذ البقرة عندما ينام صاحبها.»
english_before: “I will take the cow after her owner sleeps,” said the thief.
english_after: “I will take the cow after her owner sleeps,” said the thief.

arabic: وقال الشيطان: «وأنا سأخطف الرجل نفسه.»
english_before: “And I will take the man himself,” said the devil.
english_after: “And I will take the man himself,” said the devil.

arabic: رأى الاثنان أن الوقت مناسب،
english_before: Both thought the moment was right,
english_after: Both thought the moment was right,

arabic: فاتفقا على الانتظار حتى يطفئ الناسك المصباح ويستريح.
english_before: so they agreed to wait until the ascetic put out the lamp and rested.
english_after: so they agreed to wait until the ascetic put out the lamp and rested.

arabic: دخل الناسك بيته، وربط البقرة في زاوية،
english_before: The ascetic went inside, tied the cow in a corner,
english_after: The ascetic went inside, tied the cow in a corner,

arabic: وتناول عشاءه ثم نام.
english_before: ate his supper, and fell asleep.
english_after: ate his supper, and fell asleep.

arabic: تسلل اللص والشيطان إلى الداخل.
english_before: The thief and the devil slipped in.
english_after: The thief and the devil slipped in.

arabic: لكن قبل أن يتحرك أحدهما، بدأ بينهما خلاف حول من يبدأ أولًا.
english_before: But before either moved, they began arguing over who should go first.
english_after: But before either moved, they began arguing over who should go first.

arabic: قال الشيطان: «دعني أخطف الرجل أولًا.
english_before: The devil said, “Let me take the man first.
english_after: The devil said, “Let me take the man first.

arabic: إن أخذت البقرة قبلي فقد تستيقظ وتصدر صوتًا،
english_before: If you take the cow before me, she may wake up and make a noise.
english_after: If you take the cow before me, she may wake up and make a noise.

arabic: فينهض الناسك ولا أستطيع أخذه.»
english_before: Then the ascetic will rise, and I cannot take him.”
english_after: Then the ascetic will rise, and I cannot take him.”

arabic: لكن اللص رفض أن ينتظر.
english_before: But the thief refused to wait.
english_after: But the thief refused to wait.

arabic: رد اللص: «بل دعني أسرق البقرة أولًا!
english_before: The thief replied, “No, let me steal the cow first!
english_after: The thief replied, “No, let me steal the cow first!

arabic: إذا حاولت خطف الرجل فربما يستيقظ،
english_before: If you try to abduct the man, he may wake up.
english_after: If you try to abduct the man, he may wake up.

arabic: وعندها لن أستطيع الخروج بالبقرة.»
english_before: Then I cannot leave with the cow.”
english_after: Then I cannot leave with the cow.”

arabic: ارتفع صوتاهما شيئًا فشيئًا، ولم يرضَ أي منهما بالتراجع.
english_before: Their voices grew louder, and neither would give way.
english_after: Their voices grew louder, and neither would give way.

arabic: وفجأة صرخ اللص: «أيها الناسك، استيقظ!
english_before: Suddenly the thief shouted, “Ascetic, wake up!
english_after: Suddenly the thief shouted, “Ascetic, wake up!

arabic: هناك شيطان يريد خطفك!»
english_before: A devil wants to abduct you!”
english_after: A devil wants to abduct you!”

arabic: فصرخ الشيطان أيضًا: «استيقظ! هذا لص يريد سرقة بقرتك!»
english_before: The devil shouted too, “Wake up! This is a thief trying to steal your cow!”
english_after: The devil shouted too, “Wake up! This is a thief trying to steal your cow!”

arabic: سمع الناسك الصياح، ففتح عينيه ونهض بسرعة.
english_before: The ascetic heard the yelling, opened his eyes, and jumped up.
english_after: The ascetic heard the yelling, opened his eyes, and jumped up.

arabic: جاء الجيران بعدما سمعوا الضجة،
english_before: The neighbors came when they heard the commotion,
english_after: The neighbors came when they heard the commotion,

arabic: فهرب اللص والشيطان دون أن يأخذا شيئًا.
english_before: and the thief and the devil fled empty-handed.
english_after: and the thief and the devil fled empty-handed.

arabic: بقي الناسك في بيته وبقرته إلى جانبه.
english_before: The ascetic stayed in his home with his cow beside him.
english_after: The ascetic stayed in his home with his cow beside him.

arabic: كان الاثنان قد اقتربا من النجاح، لكن خلافهما أنقذ الرجل.
english_before: Both intruders had been close to success, but their quarrel saved the man.
english_after: Both intruders had been close to success, but their quarrel saved the man.

arabic: كان رجل يعمل خادمًا عند أحد الأغنياء،
english_before: A man worked as a servant for a wealthy person,
english_after: A man worked as a servant for a wealthy person,

arabic: ثم قرر أن يترك عمله ويسافر.
english_before: then decided to leave his job and travel.
english_after: then decided to leave his job and travel.

arabic: أعطاه صاحب العمل دينارين أجرًا له.
english_before: His employer gave him two dinars in wages.
english_after: His employer gave him two dinars in wages.

arabic: أراد الرجل أن يتصدق بدينار، وأن يحتفظ بالآخر لطعامه في الطريق.
english_before: The man wanted to give one dinar in charity and keep the other for food on the road.
english_after: The man wanted to give one dinar in charity and keep the other for food on the road.

arabic: دخل السوق فرأى صيادًا يبيع هدهدين ضعيفين في قفص واحد.
english_before: He entered the market and saw a hunter selling two weak hoopoes in one cage.
english_after: He entered the market and saw a hunter selling two weak hoopoes in one cage.

arabic: سأل عن ثمنهما، فقال الصياد: «ديناران.»
english_before: He asked their price, and the hunter said, “Two dinars.”
english_after: He asked their price, and the hunter said, “Two dinars.”

arabic: حاول أن يشتريهما بدينار واحد،
english_before: He tried to buy both for one dinar,
english_after: He tried to buy both for one dinar,

arabic: لكن الصياد رفض.
english_before: but the hunter refused.
english_after: but the hunter refused.

arabic: فكر الرجل أن يشتري طائرًا واحدًا ويترك الآخر.
english_before: The man considered buying one bird and leaving the other.
english_after: The man considered buying one bird and leaving the other.

arabic: ثم خاف أن يكون الهدهدان زوجين، وأن يفرقهما عن بعضهما.
english_before: Then he feared they might be a pair and he would separate them.
english_after: Then he feared they might be a pair and he would separate them.

arabic: أشفق عليهما، ودفع الدينارين معًا،
english_before: He felt compassion, paid both dinars,
english_after: He felt compassion, paid both dinars,

arabic: ولم يبقَ معه شيء من أجره.
english_before: and had none of his wages left.
english_after: and had none of his wages left.

arabic: لم يرد أن يطلق الطائرين وسط السوق؛
english_before: He did not want to release the birds in the market:
english_after: He did not want to release the birds in the market:

arabic: فقد كانا جائعين وضعيفين، وربما أمسك بهما صياد آخر.
english_before: they were hungry and weak, and another hunter might catch them.
english_after: they were hungry and weak, and another hunter might catch them.

arabic: سار بهما إلى أرض بعيدة فيها أشجار كثيرة،
english_before: He walked to a distant place full of trees
english_after: He walked to a distant place full of trees

arabic: وفتح القفص برفق.
english_before: and gently opened the cage.
english_after: and gently opened the cage.

arabic: طار الهدهدان بصعوبة حتى وصلا إلى شجرة مثمرة.
english_before: The two hoopoes flew with difficulty to a fruit tree.
english_after: The two hoopoes flew with difficulty to a fruit tree.

arabic: جلسا فوق غصن، وشكرا الرجل لأنه أنقذهما.
english_before: They perched on a branch and thanked the man for rescuing them.
english_after: They perched on a branch and thanked the man for rescuing them.

arabic: ثم قال أحدهما للآخر: «علينا أن نكافئه.
english_before: Then one said to the other, “We must reward him.
english_after: Then one said to the other, “We must reward him.

arabic: تحت هذه الشجرة جرّة مليئة بالذهب.»
english_before: Beneath this tree is a jar full of gold.”
english_after: Beneath this tree is a jar full of gold.”

arabic: سمع الرجل كلامهما ودهش. سألهما: «كيف عرفتما مكان ذهب مخفي تحت الأرض،
english_before: The man heard them and was astonished. He asked, “How did you know about gold hidden underground,
english_after: The man heard them and was astonished. He asked, “How did you know about gold hidden underground,

arabic: ولم تريا شبكة الصياد التي أمسكت بكما؟»
english_before: yet fail to see the hunter’s net that caught you?”
english_after: yet fail to see the hunter’s net that caught you?”

arabic: أجاب أحد الهدهدين: «حين يأتي القدر،
english_before: One hoopoe answered, “When destiny arrives,
english_after: One hoopoe answered, “When destiny arrives,

arabic: قد تغيب عن العيون أشياء واضحة.»
english_before: even obvious things may be hidden from our eyes.”
english_after: even obvious things may be hidden from our eyes.”

arabic: حفر الرجل عند أصل الشجرة، حتى وجد جرّة من الفخار.
english_before: The man dug beside the tree until he found a clay jar.
english_after: The man dug beside the tree until he found a clay jar.

arabic: فتحها، فإذا هي مليئة بالدنانير الذهبية.
english_before: He opened it and discovered it was full of gold dinars.
english_after: He opened it and discovered it was full of gold dinars.

arabic: شكر الهدهدين ودعا لهما بالسلامة،
english_before: He thanked the two hoopoes and wished them well,
english_after: He thanked the two hoopoes and wished them well,

arabic: ثم حمل الكنز وعاد به.
english_before: then carried the treasure away.
english_after: then carried the treasure and went back with it.

arabic: وبعد وقت، أخبر الرجل ملك البلاد بما حدث،
english_before: Later the man told the king what had happened
english_after: Later the man told the king what had happened

arabic: وعرض أن يضع الذهب في خزينة القصر.
english_before: and offered to place the gold in the royal treasury.
english_after: and offered to place the gold in the royal treasury.

arabic: لكن الملك قال له: «احتفظ به، فهو لك.»
english_before: But the king said, “Keep it. It belongs to you.”
english_after: But the king said, “Keep it. It belongs to you.”

arabic: فخرج الرجل من عند الملك والذهب معه، يتذكر الطائرين.
english_before: The man left the king carrying the gold, remembering the two birds.
english_after: The man left the king carrying the gold, remembering the two birds.
